questions.q: Why does the defect-model-server Deployment start with replicas: 1 even though the lab's whole point is scale-to-zero?
options: It's a typo and should be replicas: 0
Kubernetes requires at least one replica in every Deployment manifest forever
KEDA, not the Deployment spec, owns the actual replica count once the ScaledObject is applied -- the starting value is temporary
replicas: 1 is required for the readiness probe to function at all
questions.explain: Once the ScaledObject is wired in, KEDA manages the Deployment's replica count directly, including taking it to zero -- the manifest's starting value stops mattering.

questions.q: What question does the queue-depth trigger in this lab's ScaledObject answer, versus the GPU-utilization trigger?
options: Both triggers answer the exact same question redundantly
The queue-depth trigger answers whether any replica should exist at all (0 to 1); the GPU-utilization trigger answers whether the warm replica is saturated enough to add more (1 to many)
The GPU-utilization trigger controls scale-to-zero, and queue depth controls scaling beyond one replica
Neither trigger has anything to do with replica count
questions.explain: The two triggers split the problem cleanly: one governs the zero floor, the other governs scaling above a single warm replica.

questions.q: What does cooldownPeriod: 300 actually control in the ScaledObject?
options: How long a pod has to pass its readiness probe before serving traffic
How many GPUs a single replica can request
The timeout for the Ingress TLS certificate renewal
How long KEDA waits during an idle window before scaling replicas back down to zero, trading a little idle cost for fewer cold starts
questions.explain: cooldownPeriod is the deliberate buffer that keeps a short lull between bursts from triggering a fresh cold start on the very next request.

questions.q: Why doesn't this lab attach a PodDisruptionBudget with minAvailable: 1 to the scale-to-zero endpoint?
options: PodDisruptionBudgets are only supported for StatefulSets
minAvailable: 1 can't be guaranteed on an endpoint that's deliberately allowed to run zero replicas -- the two are in direct tension
The endpoint doesn't use a Service, so a PDB wouldn't apply
PodDisruptionBudgets are deprecated in current Kubernetes versions
questions.explain: A PDB's minimum-available guarantee cannot coexist with a scaler whose whole point is legitimately running zero replicas some of the time.

questions.q: What does a clean end-to-end test of this endpoint show, according to the lab?
options: Replicas stay at a constant 2 the entire time, regardless of traffic
Replicas only ever go from 0 to 1 and never scale further
Zero replicas while idle, exactly one replica after the first request's cold start clears, and more than one replica once GPU utilization crosses 70% under sustained load
The Ingress returns an error whenever replicas are at zero
questions.explain: A correct test demonstrates both halves of the scaler working: the zero-to-one cold start and the one-to-many GPU-utilization scale-up under real load.
